A. Adoption of the Second Year of the FY 2023-25 Biennial Budget, Adoption of the First Year and Approval of the Second Year of the FY 2024-26 Biennial Capital Improvement Program Budget
Recommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council, Housing Authority and Parking Authority:
1. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica adopting the FY 2024-25 Operating Budget and adopting the first year and approving the second year of the FY 2024-26 Biennial Capital Improvement Program Budget at Attachment A, as amended by Attachment D;
2. Adopt a Resolution of the Housing Authority of the City of Santa Monica adopting the FY 2024-25 Operating Budget and adopting the first yea r and approving the second year of the FY 2024-26 Biennial Capital Improvement Program Budget at Attachment B, as amended by Attachment D; and
3. Adopt a Resolution of the Parking Authority of the City of Santa Monica adopting the FY 2024-25 Operating Budget and adopting the first year and approving the second year of the FY 2024-26 Biennial Capital Improvement Program Budget at Attachment C, as amended by Attachment D.
Staff also recommends that the City Council:
4. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica revising the City’s master fee schedule to establish and revise certain permit and user fees and charges (Attachment E);
5. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica revising the City’s master fine schedule to establish and revise the administrative citation schedule of fines for certain violations of the Santa Monica Municipal Code (Attachment F);
6. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica establishing parking rates and permit fees for all City parking facilities and resources (Attachment G);
7. Adopt a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Santa Monica temporarily waiving and reducing outdoor dining license fees for third street promenade to stimulate economic recovery (Attachment H);
8. Adopt a Resolution of the City of Santa Monica establishing new classifications and adopting salary rates for various listed positions (Attachment I) and approve the position and classification changes (Attachment J);
9. Adopt a Resolution of the City of Santa Monica establishing the Gann appropriations limit for FY 2024-25 (Attachment K);
10. Adopt a Resolution incorporating a project funded by SB1: The Road Repair and Accountability Act (Attachment L);
11. Adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Mana ger to revise the Confidential Unrepresented Employee (CUE) Pay Plan (Attachment M)
12. Maintain existing adult-use and medicinal cannabis tax rates or provide direction to staff on the desired adult-use and medicinal tax rate increases and adopt a resolution increasing the adult-use and medicinal cannabis tax rates as directed effective January 1, 2025 (Attachment N);
13. Authorize the City Manager to accept a discretionary grant award in the amount of $50,000 from the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority and approved by Supervisorial District 3 to support the City Attorney’s Office Shelter, Treatment, and Empowerment Program (STEP) Court;
14. Authorize the City Manager to accept a grant award of $4,822,406 from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development ’s Continuum of Care Program to provide housing subsidies for the homeless and disabled population and to execute all necessary documents to accept the grant and any subsequent renewals;
15. Adopt a finding of no possibility of significant effect pursuant to S ection 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines; and
16. Adopt a finding that the proposed landing fee reduction project, which includes reduced rates for tie-downs, transient tie-downs, hangars, landing fees, and fuel flowage fees (Reduced Airport Fees), exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”) pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21080(b)(1) and CEQA Guidelines sections 15061(b)(3), and 15369.

B. Request of Mayor Brock, Vice Mayor Negrete, and Councilmember Davis that the City Council direct the City Attorney to prepare a resolution for Council consideration that recites that, while the City of Santa Monica is respectful of everyone’s First Amendment rights to free speech, in some instances harm can come from expression that is false and/or counter to the public interest. The resolution should reflect the Council’s disapproval of signs placed upon a building along the 3rd Street Promenade that falsely state that the City Manager approves of the County’s “free needle and meth pipe” program, as in fact the program is implemented by a contractor of Los Angeles County pursuant to state law, and the City Council and City Manager play no role in authorizing the program. Further, to the extent that there is City policy on the program, the City Council is the source of any such City policy on the subject, not the City Manager. Finally, the signs also may be counter-productive to the community’s stated goal of economic recovery as they may deter people from visiting and shopping in Santa Monica at a time when the City’s retail, travel, and entertainment businesses are still recovering from the pandemic. New Item Received. 8/6/2026

a. Written Comments
C. Request by Councilmember Parra and Mayor Brock to direct the City Manager and City Attorney to return with amendments to the Municipal Code, including a potential interim zoning ordinance, to allow in R2, R3, and R4 zone districts only front fence, wall, and hedge heights to be limited to 72” in height in the front setback, address measurements that may include retaining walls, and suspend enforcement and pending applications until the ordinance becomes effective in R2, R3, and R4 for those that would comply with that standard. New Item Received. 8/6/2026
Staff Report Printout
a. Written Comments
D. Request of Councilmembers Zwick and Torosis that, upon the expansion of Santa Monica’s Preserving Our Diversity (POD) program, the City Manager take steps to address historic underrepresentation of Pico Neighborhood residents in the program relative to the community’s percentage of residents over 65 experiencing poverty. Specifically, this should include: New Item Received. 8/6/2026
1. Enhancing the Housing and Human Service Department’s outreach plan through partnerships with local faith- based and community-serving organizations including but not limited to Familias Latinas Unidas, St. Anne’s, Calvary Baptist, The Venice Family Clinic on Pico, the Pico Neighborhood Association, and the senior programming and food pantry at Virginia Avenue Park.
2. Offering direct technical assistance with filling out the POD program application at Virginia Avenue Park.
3. Assessing the Jan 1, 2000 habitation requirement as well as other eligibility criteria, with the authority to make the program more flexible and expansive.
4. Give preference to applications from census tracts designated as “disadvantaged” by the state under SB 535 Disa d vantaged Communities , subject to any limitations imposed by state and federal fair housing laws, in consultation with the City Attorney’s Office.
5. Authorizing up to 5% of newly designated program resources to be spent on enhanced outreach and technical assistance in the Pico Neighborhood, if necessary.
Staff Report Printout
a. Written Comments
E. Request of Mayor Brock that the City Attorney and City Manager return to City Council no later than July 23, 2024 with a proposal to place a parcel tax measure on the November 2024 ballot to generate resources to address public safety and homelessness. More specifically, the proposed parcel tax should generate $7.5 million per year and allow for resources generated by the tax to support items such as enhanced police services, private security in downtown, and multidisciplinary outreach teams. The tax should also have a sunset date 10 years after its effective date. New Item Received. 8/6/2026
